reviews.title: Critical Feedback: Significant Improvements Needed in Lesson Structure and Quiz Design
reviews.text:
Assalamu Alaikum,

I want to share some constructive but critical feedback on the educational experience in the Jibreel app.

I appreciate Jibreel's mission and the effort to make Islamic education accessible, engaging, and convenient. However, after completing lessons and taking the accompanying quizzes, I have become increasingly frustrated with what I perceive as a disconnect between the information being taught and the questions being asked.

My biggest concern is that some quiz questions appear to assess information that was not clearly explained or sufficiently emphasized in the preceding lesson. I have carefully reviewed the material and still encountered questions that require knowledge or distinctions I do not recall being explicitly covered.

This creates a frustrating learning experience, particularly for Muslims who are genuinely trying to strengthen their understanding of the deen.

I understand the educational value of challenging questions, active recall, and knowledge retention. However, there is an important difference between challenging someone to apply what they have learned and expecting them to answer questions without adequate preparation.

If Jibreel’s goal is to make Islamic knowledge accessible to Muslims of varying educational backgrounds, the instructional design needs to reflect that commitment.

I would strongly encourage your development and educational teams to address the following issues:

1. Improve alignment between lessons and assessments.

reviews.text: I was excited to see this within the pillars app but so disappointed to see it doesn’t even have a free option. I hate all apps that try to hide behind a trial and have no free option. Disappointed to see the same from this app seeing how it was recommended by Pillars

reviews.title: Refused to give me a refund
reviews.text:
I signed up for the 7 day trial and forgot to cancel, and was shortly charged the entire year £59 for an app that I never used. 
Charging a full year immediately after such a short trial is very sneaky.
My refund request was rejected twice, so I contacted the developers with a heartfelt email appealing to their good nature, explaining my financial situation and asking for refund. 
They never replied. 
I eventually had to escalate with Apple customer service who were far more helpful than the developers themselves. 
The lack of communication and unwillingness to help left me feeling that this app just wanted to take my money. I do not recommend.
claimed to want to help muslims learn about the deen but charge them immediately. great! let’s take our money from peoples pockets in the name of guidance

reviews.title: Cancelled Trial but still charged for the year
reviews.text:
I signed up for the free trial, didn’t find it suitable for my needs, and cancelled within the trial period. Later, I decided to give the app another chance and signed up for a second free trial again cancelling on time but this time I was charged for a full year.

I’ve contacted support multiple times requesting a refund, but unfortunately there has been no proper resolution.

As a tech entrepreneur, I completely understand how subscription models work. That said, charging a customer for an annual plan after a cancelled trial and then refusing to prorate or offer any flexibility is not aligned with modern, customer-first SaaS practices. In most platforms, if a user has paid for a year but doesn’t continue, at least a partial refund or prorated adjustment is offered.

Regarding the product itself, the learning experience feels very rigid. You cannot skip lessons or move freely between topics you are forced to follow a fixed schedule. As a user, you have no real freedom to choose what you want to learn or focus on, which makes the experience frustrating and not personalized.

At this point, I’ve accepted the charged amount as a form of “charity,” which is disappointing.

The app has potential, but:
	•	The billing and refund process needs serious improvement
	•	The learning flow is too restrictive and not user-driven
	•	The overall experience does not justify a yearly commitment

I hope the team rethinks both their subscription handling and the product flexibility, because with

reviews.title: Great concept, wish it was free
reviews.text: After the 7 day free trial you have to subscribe to use the app, so cost is a barrier to accessing this resource unfortunately. Some people are living paycheck to paycheck and in debt. If I had the money to subscribe, I would. But when you don’t even know how you’ll afford your meals for the week, paying for any app or non-essential service feels unfeasible. I don’t have any streaming services or subscriptions in general besides $3/month for my phone storage because my phone would be unusable without it. I think the app concept is great, but this type of information should be more easily accessible to Muslims who don’t have tons of financial resources. I hope the app developers can find a way to address this barrier so that this reaches more people inshallah.

reviews.title: Sleazy marketing, sketchy app
reviews.text:
After about 300 screens you are shown that this costs money, an egregious amount. They’re marketing guilt trips you using Quran and Hadith to extract money from users. 

And they only show you the cost after you enter lots of information about yourself and your goals. 

I wouldn’t go near this app with a 10 foot pole. Smells super fishy and sketchy. Something is very wrong here. Stay away. Pretty sure this is a data collection app. 

(Otherwise a great idea, great design, but incredibly deceptive).
